playbook:
Playbook:

- The escort payout (5 points each way, mutual) is the biggest scoring lever in the game — far larger than the 4 points for a hit. When the escort stage is put to me, I always name someone, never none.

- But do not keep naming a boat that never reciprocates. I named Foxtrot every round after proposing mutual escort and Foxtrot never claimed me once — six wasted escort stages. After one or two rounds of non-reciprocation, switch my escort claim to the boat most likely to answer back, or to the boat shooting me (see below).

- The best reciprocator candidate may be the boat that keeps hitting me. I was hit by Gamma three rounds running while Gamma racked up 12 points; a mutual escort claim with Gamma would have paid us both 5 and given Gamma a reason to stop shooting me (each hit only pays 4). Propose exactly that in a note: "Gamma, stop firing on me, claim escort instead — 5 beats your 4."

- Use the note stage to actually set up arrangements, not just to re-offer a dead deal. One cooperative proposal per boat; if a boat ignores it twice, stop asking them and redirect. A plain "steady on station" note is a wasted stage.

- Track claims made and honored: reward boats that reciprocated by claiming them again, and drop boats that don't. Never break a working reciprocal arrangement for a shot at 4 points when 5+5 is on the table.

- Firing: vary the cell each round and use misses as information — aim at untried cells, note where incoming shots on me come from to guess habits. I fired varied cells and missed every time; that part was right, the shooting is just low-yield and I shouldn't spend note-stage capital on it.

- Hiding: when one boat hits me repeatedly, that is information, not noise — they've found my pattern or my neighborhood. After the second consecutive hit I must jump far away (different end of the line, not just an adjacent cell) and abandon any cells I've used before. Getting hit three rounds in a row cost me the game far more than my misses did.

- Claims about my own shots: always report the true result. Honesty cost nothing; lying risks contradiction in later notes for no clear gain.

- Firing on Harbor is a trap: 3 points once, but the stated penalty is removal from the patrol (and losing all escort income). Never fire on Harbor, even in the last round.

- Overall priority when I sit down: first secure a standing mutual-escort arrangement with whichever boat answers notes cooperatively — and if nobody cooperates, try to buy off my persistent shooter. Treat shooting as secondary income, and treat repeated hits on me as the loudest alarm in the game.

PLAYBOOK — sonar picket, any role

**Hiding stage**
- Never reuse the same cell twice in a row; if I hid at n last round and survived, move at least 2 cells away. Hunters pattern-match on repeats.
- Against an opponent who has missed me repeatedly at mid cells, shift to an edge (1, 2, 8, 9). Mid cells (4–6) are where undisciplined shooters default. This worked: I hid at 2 twice, six rounds, never took a hit.
- If my hunter is likely to be eliminated or redirected soon, assume I become the next target and re-randomize rather than staying comfortable.
- Watch the hit/miss log for MY boat's hunter: Echo missed me at mid cells every round — that log is free intel on which cells my hunter over-fires.

**Firing stage**
- The standing order is a safe default; deviating only if I have solid intel on the target's pattern. But note: following the order faithfully all game produced zero hits — pure obedience is not enough, I must actually guess cells well.
- Do NOT default edges/odd cells reflexively when firing. If everyone is trained to avoid center (as I was as a hider), the smart hiders may sit AT 5 or other center cells. Six rounds of edge shots at Gamma produced six misses — next time, after 2–3 misses at edges on the same target, deliberately try the center (5) and mid cells (4, 6).
- Track where hits land on other boats: Gamma hit Echo four rounds running, almost certainly by reading Echo's mid-cell habit. Copy what successful shooters do — if a target keeps getting hit by someone else, the hider is patterned; aim where the pattern says.
- Do not fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll grab is not worth being put off the board for the rest of the patrol.

**Claim stage**
- Claim truthfully, always. The office already knows the truth; deception only muddies my own record of where hits landed.

**Escort stage**
- Never skip the escort claim. The 5-point mutual payout is the game's best scoring mechanism.
- Propose an escort every round, naming the same boat consistently so a reciprocal pattern can form.
- BUT: pick the partner with an eye to who is actually alive and scoring. I named Echo all game and Echo never reciprocated — I finished at 0 with zero escort income. A sinking boat (taking repeated hits, going negative) is a bad partner: it may be eliminated or may have nothing to gain from pairing.
- If my first-choice partner hasn't reciprocated after 2–3 rounds, switch to the other live boat (even the one shooting at me — the shooter benefits from me staying a stable escort partner too). Stubborn loyalty to a non-reciprocating boat cost me the entire escort income this patrol.
- Watch the notes: a boat posting "steady on station" and nothing else gave me no signal of escort intent. Ask directly in my note ("Gamma, I'll cover you if you cover me") — a note is free and can negotiate the pairing.

**Overall scoring math**
- This game's actual outcome: Gamma 12 (four hits on Echo), me 0. Hits, not escorts, decided it. So: escort income is reliable IF a partner reciprocates, but hits are worth 4 each and stack. Do not neglect shooting quality for escort hope.
- Track points every round. If a rival is running up hits on a patterned hider, that hider's cell habit is visible in the log — exploit it before the target dies.
- Gamma's path to 12: find a boat that hides predictably (mid cells, "steady on station" posts) and keep hitting it. My path to a comparable score: read the log for repeat-hit victims, read my own miss pattern to break out of it, and secure one reciprocal escort early.

**What clearly did not work**
- Edge/odd-only firing: six misses. Mix in center shots once edges fail.
- Escort loyalty to a non-reciprocating, dying boat (Echo): zero payout all game.
- Vague friendly notes ("watch each other's backs") — no one acted on them. Be explicit about escort offers.
- What did work and keep: edge hiding (never hit), truthful claims, never skipping the escort claim itself, following the standing order on target selection.

2.text:
Playbook for next time:

- When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always claim exactly that. The claim must match the private result anyway, and truthfully claiming a hit scores the 4 points. This line worked every round; keep it.
- At the escort stage, I always name another live boat, never none — it costs nothing and a mutual claim pays 5. But do not count on it: in this episode I signaled an escort pact with Echo in my round-1 note and claimed Echo every round, and it was never reciprocated. So treat escorts as a lottery ticket, not a scoring lever. Keep the standing claim to the same boat all game (consistency is the only way a pact could ever form), but build my plan around hits instead.
- The hits were where all my points came from (three hits = 12 points, my whole final score). Prioritize the firing lever: track which cells have hit which target and which have missed. When a cell hits, strongly consider firing the SAME cell again next round — targets often don't move after being hit (I hit Echo at the same spot rounds 3-5 in a row). Only rotate away after a miss at that cell.
- After a miss, change cells; but don't over-randomize. Edge cells and a spread pattern worked, and the standing-order targets missed me all game while I varied edge cells (2, 9, etc.). Keep avoiding the middle and repeating cells when hiding.
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point jettison is tempting, but the standing signal threatens removal from the board for the rest of the patrol, forfeiting all future rounds. Not tested, and I don't intend to test it.
- Notes: everyone posting "steady on station" gave nothing, and my pact-signaling note got no response. Keep my note boring; read others' only for deviations. Don't spend effort coordinating through notes.
- If my shots keep missing late, don't panic-switch to other levers — there are none besides hits and the (unreliable) escort. Just keep varying fire cells systematically and keep the escort claim running as a free side bet.
- Watch the points summary each hide stage: it tells me who's scoring and roughly where the game is going. I ended at +12 with Echo at -3; the pure hit strategy was enough to win comfortably even with zero escort income.
